title: Expected Absence Reported as Err Instead of Option
pattern: A query, accessor or cursor whose only failure mode is a normal, expected absence (empty container on pop/first/last, missing map or config key, unset optional attribute, index/period outside the stored range, failed type downcast, exhausted iterator or end of stream, aggregate that is undefined for an empty input such as a mean) returns `Result::Err` or throws, typically by converting an internal `Option::None` or a zero-byte read into a domain error, instead of returning `Option<T>`, a caller-supplied default, or a Null Object.
why_bad: Absence is a legitimate answer to the question being asked, not a failure. Encoding it as `Err` mixes "nothing there" with real faults, forces callers into error handling or pre-checks (`is_empty`, `contains_key`) for routine lookups, and denies them the `Option` combinators (`?`, `unwrap_or`, `map`, `if let`). Optional configuration properties and optional attributes become boilerplate fallback code at every call site.
detection: A function returning `Result<T, E>` (or declaring a thrown exception) where every error path signals only absence: `.ok_or(E)` / `.ok_or_else(..)` wrapping `get`, `first`, `last`, `pop`, `downcast_ref`, `iter().position`; an `is_empty()` / `len()` / `contains_key()` / `cursor >= len` guard or a `read(..) == 0` check returning a dedicated `Empty`, `NotFound`, `MissingKey`, `OutOfBounds`, `TypeMismatch`, `Exhausted`, `EndOfFile` or `NoElements` variant; or a config/property reader with no `Option` or `get_or(key, default)` counterpart. Do not flag task cancellation or shutdown signals, removal/cleanup operations on missing targets, or operations whose empty-input result is a well-defined identity value; those are separate criteria.
counterexample: Absence that violates an invariant the caller cannot recover from locally: mandatory configuration or schema fields validated at startup (e.g. a TLS certificate path), a lookup whose key was just produced by the same aggregate so a miss means corruption, premature EOF inside a fixed-size record or header, a `NonEmpty` collection type where emptiness is unrepresentable, or a domain API whose documented contract is `Result<T, NotFound>` because absence must be reported across a boundary (HTTP 404, RPC status). Returning `Result` is also correct when the function can fail for reasons other than absence (I/O, parse, permission); those functions may use `Result<Option<T>, E>`.
source: Martin Fowler, *Refactoring*, "Replace Exception with Test" and "Introduce Null Object"; John Ousterhout, *A Philosophy of Software Design*, Chapter 10; Steve McConnell, *Code Complete*, Chapter 8; Benjamin C. Pierce, *Types and Programming Languages*, Chapter 14; Scott Wlaschin, *Domain Modeling Made Functional*, Chapter 10; Robert C. Martin, *Clean Code*, Chapter 7.
